summary.text: A chemical reaction turns one set of chemical substances into another by rearranging atoms, and it comes with an energy change.
The starting substances are called reactants, and the products they yield usually have properties different from them.
Some reactions produce heat, others may require heat, and reaction rates typically increase as temperature rises.

facts.label: Heat-needing reactions
facts.value: Endothermic reactions may require heat to occur

facts.label: Speed and temperature
facts.value: Rates typically increase as temperature rises

facts.label: Enzymes in cells
facts.value: Protein enzymes speed up biochemical reactions

items.prompt: A chemist mixes two clear liquids and ends up with a white solid whose properties are unlike either liquid. What are the two clear liquids called in chemistry?

options.label: Products
Reactants
Elementary steps
Mechanisms

items.explain: The substances that start a reaction are reactants, and they yield products that usually have different properties.

items.prompt: Cracking open a pocket hand warmer makes it feel hot in your glove. Which kind of reaction best matches this?

options.label: Endothermic, because the reaction requires heat
Neither, because the atoms only move around
Nuclear, because heat means the nuclei changed
Exothermic, because the reaction produces heat

items.explain: Reactions that produce heat are called exothermic; those that may require heat are endothermic.

items.prompt: A cook raises the burner under a pot of stew. Usually, what happens to how fast the reactions in the stew go?

options.label: They speed up, as more thermal energy is available
They slow down, as extra heat keeps bonds intact
They stay put, as only the pot's heat changes
They halt, as bonds cannot break when it is hot

items.explain: Typically reaction rates increase with temperature, because more thermal energy is available to reach the activation energy for breaking bonds.

items.prompt: Your body breaks down food at body temperature, far milder than a furnace. What lets those reactions happen so readily in your cells?

options.label: Intense heat built up inside each cell
Atoms turning into other elements
Protein enzymes that raise reaction rates
Phlogiston released from the food

items.explain: Reactions in biochemistry are often catalyzed by protein enzymes, which increase reaction rates so they can occur at the temperature and concentrations within a cell.

items.prompt: In the 1600s a popular theory said a fire-like substance hidden inside burnable things escapes when they burn. What did Antoine Lavoisier find instead in 1785?

options.label: Burning splits matter into four basic elements
Burning is a reaction with oxygen in the air
Burning frees a second, hidden fire-like element
Burning drains the vital force from the matter

items.explain: The phlogiston theory was proved false in 1785 when Lavoisier found that combustion is a reaction with oxygen from the air.

items.prompt: Two chemists sketch an experiment on paper. Where do the starting substances belong in a chemical equation?

options.label: On the left of the arrow
On the right of the arrow
Above the arrow
Below the arrow

items.explain: An equation shows the reactants on the left and the products on the right, separated by an arrow.
